circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.title: Exercise: build the inner ring
circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.line: Tap the relative minor of each major key to fill the inner ring

circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.title: Exercise: key to signature
circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.line: Given a key, tap how many sharps or flats it has, then tap its notes on the staff

circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.title: Exercise: neighbours
circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.line: Given a key, tap its two neighbours and its opposite key on the wheel

circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.title: Exercise: build the outer ring
circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.line: Tap the keys a fifth apart, clockwise from C, to fill the outer ring

circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.title: Exercise: add the sharps and flats
circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.line: Tap or type how many sharps or flats each key has, going round the wheel

circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.title: Exercise: signature to key
circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_e.line: Given a signature on the staff, tap its major key and its relative minor on the wheel

circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_o.title: The circle of fifths
circle_of_fifths/resources/html/circle_o.line: Click a key to see its signature, its scale on the keys and its neighbours; Play sounds the scale

circle_of_fifths/resources/images/circle.title: The circle of fifths
circle_of_fifths/resources/images/circle.line: Twelve keys, a fifth apart, closing into a ring

music_instruments/resources/html/guitar_.title: Guitar fretboard
music_instruments/resources/html/guitar_.line: Click positions from the open strings to fret 12 to hold them, then play them together, up or down

music_instruments/resources/html/interva.title: Ear exercise: both at once
music_instruments/resources/html/interva.line: Two notes sound together and the lower one is lit; find the higher one

music_instruments/resources/html/interva.title: Ear exercise: one after the other
music_instruments/resources/html/interva.line: Two notes sound in turn and the first is lit; find the second on the keyboard

music_instruments/resources/html/interva.title: Ear exercise: triads
music_instruments/resources/html/interva.line: A three-note chord sounds and the lowest note is lit; find the other two

music_instruments/resources/html/lute_fr.title: Lute fretboard
music_instruments/resources/html/lute_fr.line: Click positions to hold them and play them together, up or down; change the tuning and watch the frets stay straight or break into a zigzag

music_instruments/resources/html/mandoli.title: Mandolin fretboard
music_instruments/resources/html/mandoli.line: Click positions to hold them, play them together, up or down, and switch the tuning; the held notes are also written on a staff

music_instruments/resources/html/monocho.title: Monochord
music_instruments/resources/html/monocho.line: Move the bridge along the string, pluck either segment or both, and read the length ratio

music_instruments/resources/html/piano_k.title: Piano keyboard
music_instruments/resources/html/piano_k.line: Click keys from C3 to C5 to hold them, then play them together, up or down; the menu changes the tuning

music_instruments/resources/html/rhythm_.title: Rhythm box
music_instruments/resources/html/rhythm_.line: Click steps for kick, snare and hi-hat, press Play, and shape the groove with tempo, swing and the four banks

music_instruments/resources/html/tune_sh.title: One tune, different starting notes
music_instruments/resources/html/tune_sh.line: The notes change; the gaps between them stay

music_instruments/resources/html/whole_h.title: Whole steps and half steps
music_instruments/resources/html/whole_h.line: Click two keys to see the gap between them in whole steps and half steps

notes/resources/images/accidental.svg.title: Natural, sharp and flat
notes/resources/images/accidental.svg.line: Middle C, then C♯ and C♭: a sharp sign nudges the note up a semitone, a flat sign down

notes/resources/images/enharmonic.svg.title: C♯ and D♭
notes/resources/images/enharmonic.svg.line: Two names for the same sound, written side by side on the staff

notes/resources/images/fifths_score.svg.title: C and G
notes/resources/images/fifths_score.svg.line: Middle C and the G above it, a fifth apart on the staff

notes/resources/images/nice_score.svg.title: C and the C above
notes/resources/images/nice_score.svg.line: Middle C and the C an octave above it on the staff

notes/resources/images/note_name.svg.title: The seven natural notes
notes/resources/images/note_name.svg.line: C D E F G A B in order from middle C on the staff

notes/resources/images/pitch_class_score.title: Three Cs
notes/resources/images/pitch_class_score.line: C3, C4 and C5 on the staff: three octaves, one pitch class

notes/resources/images/semitone_score.sv.title: C and C♯
notes/resources/images/semitone_score.sv.line: A semitone on the staff: C, then the same line with a sharp sign

notes/resources/images/ugly_score.svg.title: C and D♭
notes/resources/images/ugly_score.svg.line: C4 and D♭4, a single semitone apart, on the staff

scales/resources/html/scale_build_major..title: Exercise: major scales
scales/resources/html/scale_build_major..line: Pick a tonic, tap the keys of the scale and watch the staff fill in; Play lets you hear it; finished scales stay on the shelf

scales/resources/html/scale_build_modes_.title: Exercise: modes and minor scales
scales/resources/html/scale_build_modes_.line: Pick a tonic and a scale, tap its keys and watch the staff fill in; Play lets you hear it; finished scales stay on the shelf

scales/resources/html/scale_build_natura.title: Exercise: natural minor
scales/resources/html/scale_build_natura.line: Pick a tonic, tap the keys of the scale and watch the staff fill in; Play lets you hear it; finished scales stay on the shelf

scales/resources/html/scale_build_other_.title: Exercise: pentatonic, blues and more
scales/resources/html/scale_build_other_.line: Pick a tonic and a scale, tap its keys and watch the staff fill in; Play lets you hear it; finished scales stay on the shelf

scales/resources/html/scale_ear_build_th.title: Exercise: build any scale
scales/resources/html/scale_ear_build_th.line: Pick a tonic and a scale, tap its keys and watch the staff fill in; Play lets you hear it; finished scales stay on the shelf

scales/resources/html/scale_ear_name_the.title: Ear exercise: name the scale
scales/resources/html/scale_ear_name_the.line: You hear a scale; name it

scales/resources/html/scale_player.html.title: Scale player
scales/resources/html/scale_player.html.line: Pick a tonic and a scale, press Play, and see and hear it on the keys and the staff

scales/resources/images/c_major_scale.sv.title: C major
scales/resources/images/c_major_scale.sv.line: The white keys from C to C, no sharps or flats

scales/resources/images/f_major_scale.sv.title: F major
scales/resources/images/f_major_scale.sv.line: The same recipe from F; the fourth note is B♭

scales/resources/images/g_major_scale.sv.title: G major
scales/resources/images/g_major_scale.sv.line: The same recipe from G; the seventh note is F♯

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_equ.title: C to C in equal temperament
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_equ.line: The white keys C3 to C4 are held and tuned to Equal; press Play ascending and listen

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_equ.title: A fifth in equal temperament
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_equ.line: C3 and G3 are held and tuned to Equal; press Play together, then switch to Pythagorean and play the same two keys

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_equ.title: The wolf in equal temperament
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_equ.line: G♯3 and D♯4 are held and tuned to Equal; press Play together, then switch to Pythagorean and play the same two keys

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_mea.title: C to C in meantone
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_mea.line: The white keys C3 to C4 are held and tuned to quarter-comma meantone; press Play ascending and listen

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_mea.title: The wolf in meantone
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_mea.line: G♯3 and D♯4 are held and tuned to meantone; press Play together, then switch to Equal and play the same two keys

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_mea.title: A major chord in meantone
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_mea.line: C4, E4 and G4 are held and tuned to meantone; press Play together, then switch to Pythagorean and play the chord again

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_pyt.title: C to C in Pythagorean tuning
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_pyt.line: The white keys C3 to C4 are held and tuned to Pythagorean; press Play ascending and listen

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_pyt.title: The wolf in Pythagorean tuning
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_pyt.line: G♯3 and D♯4 are held and tuned to Pythagorean; press Play together, then switch to Equal and play the same two keys

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_pyt.title: A fifth in Pythagorean tuning
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_pyt.line: C3 and G3 are held and tuned to Pythagorean; press Play together, then switch to Equal and play the same two keys

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_wel.title: C to C in well temperament
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_wel.line: The white keys C3 to C4 are held and tuned to Werckmeister III; press Play ascending and listen

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_wel.title: D to A in well temperament
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_wel.line: D4 and A4 are held and tuned to Werckmeister III; press Play together, then hold E4 and B4 and compare the two fifths

tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_wel.title: E to B in well temperament
tuning/resources/html/piano_keyboard_wel.line: E4 and B4 are held and tuned to Werckmeister III; press Play together, then switch to Equal and play the same two keys
